title: Opportunistic Accelerator Sourcing Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook documents a lightweight, repeatable process for opportunistic accelerator (GPU/TPU-like) purchases that supplement our committed orders. The intent is to safely capture short lead-time buying windows, discounted spot inventory, and third-party lease offers without destabilizing runway or runway forecasting accuracy.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to non-core committed capacity (buffer and surge lanes), not to reserved Dedicated customer pools unless explicitly approved by ICPO/Finance.
- Focus on discrete order lines up to 20% of next-quarter forecasted consumption per region. Larger buys require Exec approval.
- We assume vendors may offer partial shipments, rework/refurb units, or lease-to-buy options.

When to consider an opportunistic purchase (trigger checklist):
- Vendor contact reports a firm limited SKU lot with price >= 10% below our latest benchmark AND lead time <= 6 weeks for partial shipments.
- Short-term forecast delta (14–42 days) + regional spike (>15% above baseline) with projected token-hour burn that exceeds committed capacity.
- Lease offers where monthly lease cost < 35% of amortized monthly capex for equivalent SKU and includes swap-on-failure SLA.
- Inventory arbitrage: refurbished units with validated performance profile and vendor-return window.

Decision matrix (quick):
- Cost delta: >10% savings -> prioritize; 0–10% consider with strong lead time; negative -> reject.
- Lead time: <6 wks -> opportunistic; 6–12 wks -> conditional (hold until confirm); >12 wks -> route to Normal Procurement.
- Region fit: local inventory preferred for latency-sensitive customers; cross-region buys require transport/time margin.
- Compatibility: must be validated (quantization/perf) by Applied ML within 5 business days for core LLM profiles (long-seq).

Operational flow (6 steps):
1) Intake: Vendor contact or internal scout posts a short note in #infra-procurement with key fields (SKU, qty, price, lead time, partial ship allowed, refurb? lease?).
2) Triage (on-call infra-procurement engineer): Validate basic commercial sanity, update the Opportunistic Pipeline spreadsheet row, and assign an evaluator.
3) Eval (Applied ML + Runtime perf): Quick perf sanity (within 5 business days): microbenchmarks (latency @ 512, throughput @ batch 16, memory/KV behavior). If fail -> reject.
4) Finance & Legal check: Confirm payment terms, customs impact, VAT, return window, and warranty coverage. Clean check takes up to 3 business days.
5) Purchase decision: If passes evals and checks and fits decision matrix, Purchase Owner issues PO or signs lease. For buys >15% of quarter forecast, require Head of Infra sign-off.
6) Intake to Staging: Partial shipments enter Staging Rack policy; inbound units tagged, imaged, assigned a transient capacity ID, and flagged for post-arrival performance validation before accepting into production.

Lead-time tracking and risk controls (text matrix):
- Vendor-reported lead time = starting point. Apply SLA buffer per vendor: Tier A (OEM direct) +3 days, Tier B (reseller/refurbisher) +10 business days, Tier C (third-party lease) +14 business days.
- If vendor offers partial shipments, require minimum viable partiality: >=25% of line and no more than 3 partial shipments unless explicitly arranged.
- Staging window: any opportunistic unit held in Staging >21 days must be escalated (possible test-fail or docs missing).

Example scenarios (worked examples):
1) Short lead-time discount: Vendor X offers 200 x A450S equivalent, price -12%, lead time 28 days, partial allowed. Forecast delta in US-west is +18% in 28 days. Applied ML validates throughput parity on sample 4 units. Finance ok on terms. Decision: Approve 120 units (60% of lot) with staging hold for remaining 80 until final QC.
2) Lease fallback: Vendor Y offers 100 units on 6-month lease at $12k/mo (swap SLA). Our amortized monthly capex equivalent is $32k/mo. Lease considered if shortfall < 12 weeks and swap SLA acceptable. Use lease for 12 weeks then re-evaluate.

Inventory annotations to add on receipt (staging checklist):
- Serial tag and vendor batch id
- Firmware / BIOS version and recorded changes
- Burn-in test (4 hours) with synthetic load and KV cache exercise
- Microbenchmark results appended to row in pipeline sheet
- Assign transient pool label (e.g., OPP-Q2-25-WEST-1)

Rollout policy for opportunistic capacity:
- By default, keep comingled test and canary usage; do not immediately assign to Dedicated customers.
- Canary policy: route <= 5% of cross-customer traffic to new opportunistic SKU for 48–72 hours; monitor p95 latency, token cost delta, and error rate.
- If regressions are detected (latency +15% p95 or error rate +0.5%), halt and rollback.

Accounting and forecast integration:
- All opportunistic buys must be entered as short-term inventory on the Procurement pipeline sheet within 24 hours of PO.
- Forecast model: mark lines as "opportunistic" and use a probability weight (default 0.6) for runway calculations until 7 days post-arrival. Finance will reconcile actual vs probabilistic for month-end.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes-to-self):
- Define exact threshold for amortized monthly capex comparison for lease decisions (is 35% still right?).
- Need standard test harness for refurbished units (Elena to propose by 2025-03-15).
- Cross-region transport SLA assumptions for air vs ocean freight (Tomás to mock scenarios).

Action items (owner + ETA):
- Marcus: add opportunistic pipeline tab to infra-runway sheet and expose API to Jira (ETA 2025-02-20)
- Elena: propose refurbished burn-in test spec (ETA 2025-03-15)
- Jing: vendor buffer table (Tier mapping) consolidation (ETA 2025-02-18)
- Asha (owner): validate lease comparison calc with Finance and publish final threshold (ETA 2025-03-07)

Appendix — quick vendor buffer reference (text):
- OEM-direct: buffer 3 days; partial allowed; returns limited to 7 days post-first ship.
- Refurbisher: buffer 10 business days; require refurbishment cert and 30-day return window.
- Lease-provider: buffer 14 business days; swap-on-failure SLA required; minimum lease term 6 weeks.

Contextual links and refs: see linked artifacts at top. Add any new vendor quote links to the sheet row and ping #infra-procurement.

Notes to reviewers: this is a living doc. Primary goal: capture playbook language so on-call engineers can move quickly while preserving financial and SRE guardrails. Looking for feedback on threshold numbers and rental vs buy heuristics.
